title: Line bundles
text:
Throughout, \(S\) is a scheme and all group schemes are commutative.

Definition 1 (Line bundle) Let \(X\) be a scheme. A line bundle on \(X\) is a locally free sheaf of rank 1 on \(X\), i.e. a quasi-coherent \(\cO_X\)-module \(\cL\) such that for every \(x \in X\) there exists an open neighborhood \(U \subseteq X\) of \(x\) such that \(\cL|_U \cong \cO_U\). The set of isomorphism classes of line bundles on \(X\) forms a group under tensor product, called the Picard group of \(X\), denoted \(\operatorname{Pic}(X)\).


Definition 2 (Cartier dual) Let \(G\) be a commutative \(S\)-group scheme. Its Cartier dual is the fppf sheaf of groups on \((\mathrm{Sch}/S)\) \[
G^D := \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{S\text{-gr}}(G, \mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}}), \qquad T \longmapsto \operatorname{\mathscr{H}\!\mathit{om}}_{T\text{-gr}}(G_T, \mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}}{}_{,T}).
\]


Theorem 1 (Cartier duality) Let \(G\) be a finite locally free commutative \(S\)-group scheme. Then \(G^D\) is representable by a finite locally free commutative \(S\)-group scheme, of the same rank as \(G\), and the evaluation pairing \(G \times_S G^D \to \mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}}\) induces an isomorphism \(G \xrightarrow{\sim} (G^D)^D\).


Proof. We only sketch the argument. The question is local on \(S\), so take \(S = \operatorname{Spec}R\) and \(G = \Spec A\) with \(A\) a finite projective \(R\)-module carrying a commutative and cocommutative Hopf algebra structure. Group homomorphisms \(G_T \to \mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}}{}_{,T}\) correspond to grouplike elements of \(A \otimes_R \cO(T)\), which in turn correspond to \(R\)-algebra maps \(A^\vee \to \cO(T)\), where \(A^\vee = \operatorname{\mathscr{H}\!\mathit{om}}_R(A,R)\) carries the dual Hopf algebra structure. Hence \(G^D = \Spec A^\vee\), and \(A \to A^{\vee\vee}\) is an isomorphism because \(A\) is finite projective.


Example 1 For \(n \geq 1\) we have \((\bZ/n\bZ)_S^D \cong \mu_{n,S}\): a homomorphism \(\bZ/n\bZ \to \mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}}{}_{,T}\) is determined by the image \(u \in \cO(T)^\times\) of \(1\), subject only to \(u^n = 1\). By Theorem 1, also \(\mu_{n,S}^D \cong (\bZ/n\bZ)_S\).


Remark. Over \(S = \Spec \bF_p\), the group \(\mu_p\) is infinitesimal while its dual \(\bZ/p\bZ\) is étale; so, unlike rank, connectedness is not preserved by duality.

Cross-references work as in LaTeX: Definition 2, Theorem 1, Example 1.

title: I-adic completions
text: We want to answer the following question: If \(R\) is any ring and \(I=(f_1,\ldots, f_m)\) is a finitely generated ideal in \(R\), then is the \(I\)-adic completion of \(R\) the \(f_m\)-adic completion of \((f_1,\ldots,f_{m-1})\)-adic completion of \(R\)?
